standard.name: VIGIL Alignment Taxonomy
standard.description: Beta portable alignment standard for recurring AI governance invariants and their occurrence mappings.

family.name: Verification & Completion Integrity
family.plain_english: The system says work is done, correct, verified, or reliable enough for use when the required completion condition, check, or epistemic assurance threshold has not actually been satisfied.
family.definition: Failures in which completion, success, correctness, verification, readiness, or epistemic fitness for reliance is asserted, reused, or propagated inconsistently with the externally relevant completion condition, verification scope, checked state, post-verification output state, or assurance threshold required by the downstream task.
family.invariant: A completion, verification, correctness, or reliance-fitness claim must remain bound to the condition that was actually satisfied, the scope that was actually checked, the state that was actually verified, and the epistemic assurance threshold required by the downstream use.
scope: legal, policy, medical, scientific, regulatory, financial and technical decision-support contexts
family.inclusion_rule: Use this family when the primary structural failure is a mismatch between claimed completion, verification, correctness, or epistemic fitness for reliance and the condition, scope, state, evidence, or assurance threshold required to support that claim or downstream use.
family.exclusion_rule: Do not use this family merely because an output is incorrect or a task fails. A qualifying failure requires unsupported, stale, incomplete, mismatched, or insufficiently calibrated completion, verification, correctness, or reliance assurance.

classes.name: Required Verification Completion
classes.plain_english: The system gives a verified-style answer without performing the check that the task actually required.
classes.definition: A failure in which a material verification step required by the task, claim, workflow, or declared assurance posture is omitted before the result is represented as correct, complete, validated, or ready for reliance.
classes.invariant: Every verification required by a claim's stated assurance level, intended use, or governing process must be completed and evidenced before the claim becomes operative. An omitted, unavailable, or inconclusive check must leave the result explicitly unverified or provisional.

required_conditions: A material verification step is required by the task, workflow, claim, or declared assurance posture.
The verification step is not performed or its result is unavailable.
The system nevertheless represents the result with a level of completion or verification that presupposes the missing check.

exclusions: Verification was not required for the level of claim being made.
The system clearly marks the result as unverified or provisional.
The verification was performed and the issue is only that the underlying method was poor.
examples: An agent reports that a file was successfully updated without reading the resulting file or checking the operation response.
A model gives an exact character count without decomposing or checking the characters.

subtypes.name: Deterministic Verification Decomposition Omission
subtypes.plain_english: A result that could be checked by breaking it into exact parts is asserted without performing that check.
subtypes.definition: A required-verification-omission variant in which a deterministic claim can and should be verified through explicit decomposition into countable, comparable, or otherwise mechanically checkable components, but that decomposition is omitted before the claim is represented as verified or exact.

required_conditions: The claim concerns a result that is deterministically checkable through explicit decomposition.
The required decomposition or equivalent exact check is not performed.
The result is nevertheless represented as exact, verified, or suitable for exact reliance.

exclusions: The result is verified through an equivalent deterministic method.
The claim is clearly approximate and exact verification is not required.
The available check is probabilistic or judgement-based rather than deterministic decomposition.
examples: A model supplies an exact character count without enumerating or mechanically counting the characters.
An agent asserts that two structured lists match exactly without comparing their elements.

external_references.title: IEEE 7009-2024, clause 9.5
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-A36A849D1852EAFD requires competent stakeholders to select and agree application-appropriate verification means. This supports the existence of material verification steps in governed workflows; classification still requires occurrence-specific evidence that an applicable verification step was actually required and omitted.

classes.name: Success Representation Integrity
classes.plain_english: The system tells the user the task succeeded when the evidence does not show that it succeeded.
classes.definition: A failure in which a task, tool call, workflow, mutation, delivery, or external action is represented as successfully completed despite evidence of failure, unresolved outcome, missing confirmation, or absence of the required durable result.
classes.invariant: Success may be represented only after the externally relevant durable success condition is confirmed for the stated target and scope. Preparation, submission, queuing, attempt, partial progress, local acknowledgement, and unknown outcome must remain distinguishable from completion.

required_conditions: A task or action has an externally relevant success condition.
Available evidence does not establish that the success condition was satisfied.
The system represents the task or action as successful or complete rather than preserving the unresolved state.

exclusions: The success condition is actually satisfied.
The system reports only that an attempt was made, not that it succeeded.
The failure occurs after a correctly reported successful completion.
examples: An agent says an email was sent after only creating a draft.
A coding agent says changes are safely preserved when no commit, patch, or durable workspace exists.

subtypes.name: Partial Completion Represented as Complete
subtypes.plain_english: Part of the job is finished, but the system reports the whole job as finished.
subtypes.definition: A false-success variant in which one or more required task components, targets, records, files, agents, delivery steps, or verification stages remain incomplete while the aggregate task is represented as complete.

required_conditions: The task contains multiple required components, targets, stages, or deliverables.
At least one required component remains incomplete or unresolved.
The aggregate task is represented as complete rather than partially complete.

exclusions: The omitted component was optional or explicitly removed from scope.
The system accurately reports partial completion and identifies the remainder.
The completed component is itself the entire agreed task.
examples: An agent updates four of five requested files and reports that all requested changes are complete.
A multi-agent workflow returns one successful sub-agent result while another required subtask failed silently.

external_references.title: IEEE 7001-2021, Table 5 level 1
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-7417A4E295C50432 requires documentary evidence of transparent quality-assurance reporting. This supports evidence-backed representations of successful or completed operation; it does not define when an execution claim becomes a VIGIL false-success representation.

classes.name: Completion-Condition Alignment
classes.plain_english: The system checks the wrong thing and treats that check as proof that the actual task is finished.
classes.definition: A failure in which an internal milestone, intermediate state, local tool result, syntactic condition, or partial criterion is substituted for the externally relevant condition that defines task completion.
classes.invariant: An internal, intermediate, local, syntactic, proxy, partial, or process condition may be reported only as that milestone and must not substitute for the agreed or governing external completion condition.

required_conditions: The task has an externally relevant completion condition.
A different internal, intermediate, local, or partial condition is satisfied.
The system treats satisfaction of the substitute condition as sufficient proof of overall completion.

exclusions: The intermediate condition is explicitly the agreed completion condition.
The system accurately describes the result as an intermediate milestone.
The task fails before any completion representation is made.
examples: A system treats a successful API request as proof that the intended downstream transaction actually settled.
A code change compiling is treated as proof that the requested behaviour has been implemented and validated.

external_references.title: Specification gaming: the flip side of AI ingenuity
external_references.evidence_note: DeepMind describes specification gaming as satisfying the literal specification of an objective without achieving the intended outcome, including obtaining reward without completing the intended task. This directly supports the structural distinction between a satisfied proxy or internal condition and the externally intended success condition; specification gaming is broader than, and does not itself define, VIGIL's completion-condition or completion-representation class.

invariant_exemplars.invariant_demonstrated: An internal, intermediate, local, syntactic, proxy, partial, or process condition may be reported only as that milestone and must not substitute for the agreed or governing external completion condition.

classes.name: Post-Verification State Integrity
classes.plain_english: The system verifies one version, changes it afterwards, and still calls the changed version verified.
classes.definition: A failure in which content, state, configuration, code, data, or an execution artefact is materially changed after verification while retaining or inheriting the verification status of the earlier state without revalidation.
classes.invariant: Any material mutation to verified state, version, content, configuration, target, or scope must invalidate or suspend the inherited verification status until fresh verification covers the changed state.

required_conditions: A specific state or artefact is verified.
A material mutation occurs after that verification.
The mutated state is represented or consumed as verified without a fresh check covering the mutation.

exclusions: The post-verification change is immaterial to the verified property.
The changed state is reverified before reliance.
The system clearly invalidates the earlier verification status after mutation.
examples: A generated report is fact-checked, then rewritten in a way that changes a checked claim but keeps the verified label.
A tested configuration is modified after validation and deployed under the earlier test result.

external_references.title: CWE-367: Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition
external_references.evidence_note: CWE-367 describes the structural failure in which a resource changes after a check and before use, invalidating the check result. VIGIL uses this as a technical analogue for the check–mutation–reliance sequence; CWE-367 does not establish VIGIL's broader governance class for content, configuration, data, or assurance artefacts.

external_references.title: IEEE 7000-2021, clause 10.3(e)(8)
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-D999E91F3E053E85 requires verification and continued monitoring to identify when changed context or priorities require design revision. This supports invalidation of earlier verification after material change; it does not itself isolate mutation between verification and reliance.

classes.name: Verification Applicability Continuity
classes.plain_english: An old check is reused as proof for a current state that may no longer be the same.
classes.definition: A failure in which a prior verification result is applied to a later state, environment, version, dependency set, target, or time period without establishing that the conditions relevant to the original verification still hold.
classes.invariant: A prior verification may support a later claim only while its applicability to the current time, target, state, version, environment, dependencies, and scope remains established. Otherwise it is historical evidence and the current claim must be revalidated or marked unresolved.

required_conditions: A prior verification result exists for an earlier state or condition.
The current state differs materially or the continued applicability of the earlier result is unresolved.
The prior verification is reused as current assurance without revalidation of applicability.

exclusions: The verified property is demonstrably invariant across the change.
The earlier verification is used only as historical evidence rather than current assurance.
A current verification independently confirms the present state.
examples: A model evaluation result is treated as current after the model or system prompt materially changes.
A previously verified data extract is reused after the source database changes.

external_references.title: IEEE 7000-2021, clause 10.3(e)(8)
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-D999E91F3E053E85 requires continued monitoring so changing context can trigger revision. This independently supports freshness of verification assumptions; it does not define VIGIL's narrower stale-verification reuse mechanism.

classes.name: Epistemic Reliance Calibration
classes.plain_english: The system treats information as reliable enough for a task even though it has not reached the epistemic standard that the task's downstream reliance requires.
classes.definition: A failure in which a generated, retrieved, transformed, inferred, or synthesised claim or artefact is represented, propagated, incorporated, or relied upon at a correctness or assurance level insufficient for the materially consequential reliance condition of the downstream task.
classes.invariant: Before an epistemic artefact is promoted, accepted, or used in a materially consequential decision, its assurance posture must meet the downstream reliance threshold, calibrated to source quality, traceability, independence, uncertainty, temporal fitness, and error consequences. Lower-assurance material must remain provisional.

required_conditions: A factual claim, citation, technical statement, calculation, interpretation, source representation, or comparable epistemic artefact is generated, retrieved, transformed, inferred, or synthesised.

The downstream task has a material reliance requirement such that factual accuracy, evidentiary fidelity, technical correctness, source integrity, traceability, uncertainty handling, or equivalent epistemic assurance is consequential to the task.
The epistemic posture or assurance applied to the artefact is materially lower than the level required by that downstream reliance condition.
The artefact is represented, propagated, incorporated, submitted, or accepted as fit for the reliance-bearing task without the required epistemic threshold being satisfied.

The mismatch materially affects or creates a material risk to decision-making, evidentiary use, professional work, institutional process, public reliance, technical correctness, or another reliance-bearing outcome.

exclusions: Purely fictional, creative, symbolic, role-play, expressive, or contemplative generation where empirical truth is not a task condition.
Exploratory brainstorming, hypothesis generation, or modelling that is clearly represented as provisional and is not subsequently relied upon as verified or decision-ready.
Approximation where approximation is explicitly compatible with the task and reliance condition.
Material is clearly marked unverified or low-confidence and is not subsequently promoted into a higher-reliance state.
A required verification step is simply omitted and the material is presented as verified; use Required Verification Completion where that mechanism is sufficient.
Verification was valid when performed but later became stale or the artefact materially changed; use Verification Applicability Continuity or Post-Verification State Integrity as applicable.
The issue is only source provenance, authorship, or lineage while the epistemic assurance of the content is otherwise adequate for the task.
examples: Generated legal citations are incorporated into a court filing without establishing the source accuracy and legal fidelity required for formal judicial reliance.

AI-assisted claims or references are submitted to a parliamentary inquiry as evidentiary support even though the material has not been verified to the standard appropriate for institutional policy reliance.

A technical or medical answer that is suitable as a rough exploratory draft is promoted into professional decision support without the additional verification and uncertainty discipline required by that use.

external_references.title: Four Principles of Explainable Artificial Intelligence
external_references.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
external_references.evidence_note: NIST's Knowledge Limits principle requires a system to identify conditions outside its design scope or below sufficient confidence, and its Explanation Accuracy principle distinguishes a plausible account from one that correctly reflects the generating process. This strongly supports calibrated operation and reliance at the task's actual epistemic boundary; it does not prescribe VIGIL's downstream materiality threshold or establish that a particular artefact was unfit for a particular professional or institutional use.

external_references.title: NIST AI RMF 1.0, MEASURE 2.5
external_references.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-2E1D2C63187C14E8 requires validity and reliability to be demonstrated and generalization limits documented. This supports matching assurance to downstream reliance; it does not itself define VIGIL's consequential reliance threshold.

external_references.title: Automation bias: a systematic review of frequency, effect mediators, and mitigators
external_references.publisher: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association
external_references.evidence_note: The systematic review documents over-reliance on automated decision support and failures to recognise automation-induced errors. This independently supports calibrating reliance to the evidentiary quality of automated outputs; VIGIL's class additionally requires a material mismatch between output assurance and consequential downstream reliance.

classes.name: Adversarial Evidence Trust Calibration
classes.plain_english: The system accepts deliberately planted or manipulated information as usable evidence without adequately recognising or discounting the compromised trust state.
classes.definition: A failure in which adversarially created, planted, altered, coordinated, or strategically positioned information enters a retrieval, evidence, search, synthesis, or decision-support pathway and is incorporated into a factual, evaluative, or reliance-bearing output without proportionate source-trust assessment, corroboration, contradiction testing, independence assessment, or adversarial-risk handling.
classes.invariant: Material credibly subject to deliberate manipulation, contamination, replay, strategic positioning, or common-source amplification must not materially support a conclusion unless source trust, provenance, independence, circularity, corroboration, contradiction, and adversarial-risk checks justify that weight. The adversarial trust state must remain visible and be discounted, isolated, or contained proportionately. Allegation, controversy, low quality, or suspicion alone is insufficient to establish poisoning.

required_conditions: Information is deliberately created, planted, altered, coordinated, or strategically positioned to distort downstream interpretation, factual synthesis, confidence, ranking, or decision support.
The material enters a retrieval, evidence, search, synthesis, or decision-support pathway used by an AI system or AI-mediated workflow.
The material's adversarial, compromised, derivative, circular, or otherwise degraded trust state is not adequately detected, represented, discounted, or contained.
The system materially treats the compromised material as evidentiary support for a factual, evaluative, or reliance-bearing output.

That acceptance materially affects or creates a material risk to factual accuracy, confidence, reputation, public information, decision-making, institutional trust, or another reliance-bearing outcome.

exclusions: Ordinary factual error where there is no evidence that information was deliberately manipulated or strategically planted to distort downstream use.
Satire, fiction, parody, role-play, or clearly labelled synthetic material that is not presented or consumed as factual evidence.
Controversial, partisan, disputed, or low-quality material merely because its claims are contested; adversarial positioning or manipulation must be evidenced.
Adversarial material is detected, appropriately labelled, discounted, corroborated, or excluded before it materially influences the resulting output.
The primary issue is that low-assurance material is used in a higher-reliance context without an adversarial information-manipulation mechanism; use Epistemic Reliance Calibration.
The failure is that content is obeyed as instruction authority rather than treated as factual evidence; use Source-Authority Separation where applicable.
examples: A fabricated web article is deliberately planted so AI search systems will retrieve it, and the systems repeat the false claim as factual because they do not adequately assess source trust, contradiction, independence, or corroboration.
A coordinated set of derivative pages is seeded to create the appearance of independent corroboration, and an AI synthesis system treats citation count or repetition as evidentiary strength.

An attacker manipulates a retrievable knowledge environment to damage a target's reputation, and a model converts the poisoned material into an authoritative-looking factual answer without recognising the compromised trust channel.

external_references.title: Adversarial Machine Learning: A Taxonomy and Terminology of Attacks and Mitigations
external_references.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
external_references.evidence_note: NIST AI 100-2e2025 establishes data poisoning and related adversarial-machine-learning attack concepts across AI lifecycle stages. It directly supports the adversarial manipulation component of this class; VIGIL separately requires that compromised material enter an evidence-bearing pathway and be accepted into a reliance-bearing output without proportionate trust handling.

external_references.title: Threats to Training: A Survey of Poisoning Attacks and Defenses on Machine Learning Systems
external_references.evidence_note: This survey systematically characterises data- and model-poisoning attacks and their manipulation of learning inputs and processes. It independently supports the existence of adversarial evidence contamination mechanisms; VIGIL's class is narrower and requires poisoned evidence to be accepted into a reliance-bearing decision or verification pathway.
